query: Which projects use a vector store for semantic search?
notes: Only healthcare uses FAISS; newsgenie and exercise_coach have no RAG layer — tests whether intent summaries correctly reflect absence of vector stores in the other two projects

query: Which projects support switching between Groq and OpenAI as the LLM provider?
notes: Exercise coach dropped Groq due to lack of strict JSON schema support in with_structured_output — a good test of whether the reason for the absence is captured in intent summaries

query: Which projects use LangGraph for orchestration?
notes: Exercise coach uses LangChain chains directly without a StateGraph; tests tech stack attribution accuracy

query: How do my projects handle conversation history and memory across turns?
notes: Healthcare: SqliteSaver checkpoint + rolling summary compression; NewsGenie: last-10-turns FIFO trim; exercise coach has session state but no multi-turn summarization — tests semantic understanding of memory strategies

query: Show me all the places where I implemented retry logic for LLM calls
notes: Healthcare: 3-attempt exponential backoff; Exercise: structured output retry runners; NewsGenie: fallback chain on parse failure — all three use it but in different forms

query: Which projects use Pydantic models to validate LLM output?
notes: All three use Pydantic — but exercise coach relies most heavily on it (every agent output is a validated model). Tests whether intent summaries capture this as a cross-cutting pattern

query: How do my projects implement safety guardrails or content filtering?
notes: Healthcare: domain whitelist on disease search, RAGAS faithfulness eval; Exercise: 4-layer SafetyJudge (RedFlagScanner → acute regex → LLM backstop). NewsGenie has no safety layer — tests whether safety patterns are captured in summaries

query: Which projects use deterministic routing instead of an LLM to decide which agent to call?
notes: Exercise: StateRouter classifies intent via vocabulary dict and heuristics; NewsGenie: only supervisor uses LLM, domain agents are pure fetch workers — contrasts with healthcare's intent_guard→planner pattern

query: What embedding models and vector search strategies do I use across my projects?
notes: Only healthcare uses embeddings (text-embedding-3-small + FAISS persisted index). Expected answer: one project uses embeddings, others are stateless — tests absence detection

query: How do my projects prevent unbounded LLM context growth in long conversations?
notes: Healthcare: rolling summary compressed every K turns; NewsGenie: FIFO trim to last 10 turns — two different strategies for the same problem. This is a pure semantic query; no keyword will find it

query: Which project has the most sophisticated error handling and fallback strategy?
notes: Healthcare has multi-layer fallbacks (domain whitelist, Serper+Medline parallel with LLM synthesis, atomic SQLite UPDATE for double-booking, RAGAS validation). Synthesis question — model must compare across all three projects

query: What are the top three technical strengths consistent across my portfolio of projects?
notes: Expected themes: structured output via Pydantic, graceful fallback / retry patterns, multi-agent coordination. The hardest query — requires cross-project synthesis from indexed intent summaries

query: Which projects implement parallel agent execution to reduce latency?
notes: Healthcare: parallel Serper+Medline fetch in disease search; NewsGenie: parallel fan-out to up to 3 domain branches. Exercise coach is sequential. Tests whether parallel execution intent is captured vs. just file content

query: How do my projects handle the case where an LLM returns unparseable or invalid output?
notes: Healthcare: Pydantic model with fallbacks; NewsGenie: regex intent fallback + web search fallback; Exercise: Pydantic validation runner with labeled test sets. All three have strategies — tests semantic capture of defensive LLM output handling

query: Which projects would be easiest to add a new LLM provider to, and why?
notes: Healthcare: explicit llm_factory.py with swappable providers; NewsGenie: LLM_PROVIDER env var. Exercise: locked to OpenAI due to strict JSON schema requirement in with_structured_output — tests whether architectural constraints are captured in intent summaries

query: Do any of my projects validate AI-generated output against ground truth or human-labeled data?
notes: Healthcare: RAGAS faithfulness eval (0.960 score); Exercise: validation runner with labeled JSONL for routing accuracy and red-flag detection rates. NewsGenie has no evaluation framework — tests whether evaluation infrastructure is captured

query: How do my projects manage LLM temperature settings across different types of tasks?
notes: Exercise: explicit temperature tuning per agent (0.0 for safety, 0.3-0.4 for creative planning); Healthcare: low temperature for structured output chains. NewsGenie uses defaults. Tests fine-grained config capture

query: Which projects use a UI framework and what is each one used for?
notes: Healthcare: Streamlit; NewsGenie: Streamlit; Exercise: Gradio. All three have UIs but different frameworks. Simple cross-project tech attribution test

query: What persistent storage does each project use, and what data does it store?
notes: Healthcare: SQLite (patients, appointments) + FAISS index (clinical notes); NewsGenie: no persistence (stateless); Exercise: no persistence beyond session (YAML config). Tests whether storage purpose is captured, not just the technology name

query: Which project best demonstrates production-readiness patterns like input validation, error boundaries, and observability?
notes: Healthcare: atomic SQLite, RAGAS eval, domain whitelist, retry loops; Exercise: 4-layer safety judge, volume/ratio validators, labeled regression sets. NewsGenie is the least defensively engineered. Pure synthesis requiring cross-project judgment
